narrative.overview: The site is the inside of a railway signal box at night. The page ground is the box itself, dark green-grey; the main surfaces are an enamelled track diagram where each tunnel is a lit section running into the pixel portal from the app icon, and a lever frame below it that works the demo. Names and states are engraved black plates with cream capitals. The documentation is the box's rule book, printed on cream paper and ruled in ink.
keyCharacteristics: One dark box, one lit diagram, one lever frame; everything else stays in the box's materials.
State lives in three lamp aspects (green, amber, red), always paired with words.
Real product output (CLI transcripts, config) is the proof, shown as terminal text.
Motion is mechanical: a lever throw and a lamp changing aspect.

rules.name: The Aspect Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red mean running, changing and failed. They never decorate content, and each one always sits next to the word it means. Amber doubles as the focus ring and text selection, where it marks the one thing you are acting on.

rules.name: The Danger Plate Rule
rules.body: Red plates mark production or failure. A red plate that marks neither is a lie.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a thing is set in the plate face on a plate. Sentences are never set in capitals.

rules.name: The Real Output Rule
rules.body: Monospace appears only where the product's own text appears: commands, config, logs, ports.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Lamps glow only through their pixel halo ring drawn on the grid; no CSS glows or blurs.

dos: Do pair every aspect colour with its word.
Do show real CLI output and label demo data as a demo.
Do draw new pixel art in docs/brand/concepts/make.py and regenerate with scripts/art.py.
Do keep levers interlocked: a lever that cannot act says why.
donts: Don't add testimonials, user counts or benchmarks; there are none (PRODUCT.md, Evidence on Hand).
Don't scale pixel art by fractions or smooth it.
Don't use the aspect colours for decoration, links or headings.
Don't use monospace for anything that is not the product's own text.
